title: JOLTS Job Openings (Oct 2026)
source: BLS: bls.gov/schedule/news_release/jolts.htm, re-fetched direct 2026-09-05, reads verbatim 'October 2026 | Dec. 01, 2026 | 10:00 AM'. PROMOTED from estimate by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/jolts-2026-12-01.md, 2026-09-05), which the prior entry explicitly deferred to ('Re-read the December schedule before promoting'). Four bls.gov views now agree on 12-01: the series schedule above, bls.gov/schedule/2026/12_sched_list.htm and 12_sched.htm (both put JOLTS October-2026 data in the Dec 1 10:00 slot), and bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm, which lists NOTHING on 2026-11-30 and puts the September-data JOLTS on 11-03. The one contradicting view — the November month grid, 11_sched.htm — self-diagnoses rather than being out-voted: the same fetch reports that the grid carries a trailing row of December 1-4 and names that row's County Employment and Wages (12-02), Metropolitan Area Employment (12-02) and Employment Situation (12-04) items while omitting the Dec 1 JOLTS entry entirely, i.e. the item missing from its account of the trailing row is exactly the item it placed under 'November 30'. Residual limit, recorded rather than closed: all five views were read through a summarizing fetcher, not a verbatim HTML parse, and the ledger keeps that live as a kill switch (a bls.gov view still showing 11-30 at the next pulse demotes this back to estimate)
notes: Labor-demand read landing the same 10:00 ET slot as ISM Manufacturing (ism-manufacturing-2026-12-01, high impact), three days before jobs-2026-12-04 and eight before the fomc-2026-12-09 SEP/dot-plot meeting, with the committee already in blackout (fomc-blackout-start-2026-11-28, through 12-10). TWO FINDINGS FROM THE 2026-09-05 INITIAL RESEARCH. (1) The 10:00 pairing is measurably DAMPING, not amplifying: the one prior JOLTS+ISM-Manufacturing double (2026-09-01) printed the quietest 10:00-10:05 bar of five measured 10:00 releases (SPY 18th percentile, QQQ 8th, against each symbol's own trailing-60-session distribution), while ISM Services took the two loudest (SPY 85th on 08-05, 93rd on 09-03) — so the loud 10:00 release in this corridor is ism-services-2026-12-03, not this one. Registered as FT-jolts-2026-12-01-1; n=1, a hypothesis with a percentile behind it. (2) The date is confirmed but not immune: this print's REFERENCE MONTH is October, so government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 (estimate) sits 62 days upstream of it. In the 2025 lapse the JOLTS calendar lost a standalone release outright — the schedule page carries no Sep-2025 row and resumes at 'October 2025 | Dec. 09, 2025', a ~1-week slip — while the BLS API does carry a Sep-2025 openings value of 7,169k. A lapse relocates and consolidates this release (~12-08, i.e. FOMC day 1 and still inside blackout) without deleting the underlying data. Also refuted for this instance: the jolts-2026-09-29 sibling's 'a no-SEP FOMC raises this print's weight' argument does not transfer, because 12-09 carries the SEP and dots. Originally discovered during the chicago-pmi-2026-11-30 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05).
